title: Which Histories Stochastic Policies May Use under General Identification from Surrogate Experiments
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=incremental < floor=field and NOT salvageable in scope; bank downgraded.
gap_reasons: The exact result is confined to the one-action measured-root class, while arbitrary-ADMG necessity, fixed-alphabet countermodels, and the minimal actual-unsafety bound remain open.

Resolving oeq:general-converse requires a new fixed-alphabet completeness theorem that converts every failed arbitrary-ADMG atomic certificate into source-preserving positive countermodels and a separating policy.
The general sound-composition compiler formula is not established as written for non-ancestral later actions; repair requires integrating those actions out or enlarging the retained kernel.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved the exact safe-history frontier for a one-action binary measured-root class, including positive source-preserving twins, arbitrary-hypergraph realization, two-source selection hardness, and sharp action-count-free d-width/output-size bounds. The field-level program collapsed at the arbitrary-ADMG fixed-alphabet converse: existing gID and observational-policy completeness results do not provide the required whole-menu positive countermodels and separating policy on the declared alphabets. The general sound-composition lemma also retains a disclosed non-ancestral-action defect and must be repaired before reuse, although it does not affect the measured-root results.
tldr: Which pre-action coordinate-time histories may every stochastic policy use with a fixed menu of complete surrogate experiments? In the binary one-action class \(\mathcal R\), source coverage exactly characterizes the safe histories, gives one functional for all allowed policies, and yields one whole-menu positive rational countermodel pair on failure. A hypergraph realization gives selection hardness; the action-count-free \(d\)-coordinate certificate bound is sharp, and grouped measurements give at least \(\lfloor p/d\rfloor^d\) explicit minimal obstructions. The arbitrary-ADMG fixed-alphabet converse remains open.
gap: Existing complete results separately handle unrestricted policies from observational data and fixed interventions from complete surrogate menus; the exact safe-history frontier for the combination is not established at fixed alphabets.
fill: Prove the typed source-coverage criterion and whole-menu binary witnesses for measured roots, derive hypergraph representation and complexity results under explicit graph/source-list inputs, and separately delimit the general converse.
